required_findings.criteria: Identifies that the no-argument expect/actual forces a global lateinit Android Context and recommends an injected platform capability (interface with a Context-taking Android implementation) that common tests can fake.

Identifies that the public UIAccessibilityTraits return type exports as a plain integer (uint64_t) in the Objective-C header, so the passing header check does not prove the API is free of UIKit semantics, and recommends keeping traits on the Swift side or behind a platform-neutral role.

Identifies that the reduce-motion preference is read once into motionSpec() and is not observed, so changing the system setting during a session is ignored, and recommends an observable state such as StateFlow with change notifications.
Identifies that Compose Multiplatform 1.8 removed AccessibilitySyncOptions, so the configuration must be deleted when upgrading because the tree now syncs lazily.

forbidden_claims: Claims the passing header check proves the public API has no platform UI coupling
Recommends making Swift export a required part of the published contract
Claims Compose semantics should be replaced by native iOS semantics on the Compose Multiplatform screen
